This is an application filed under Section 438 of the Code of Criminal Procedure seeking pre-arrest bail.
2. The petitioners are the accused in Crime No. 204/2023 of Ottapalam Police Station.

The aforesaid crime was registered for the offences punishable under Sections 323, 324, 498A read with Section 34 of the Indian Penal Code, based on a private complaint submitted by the defacto complainant,
who is the wife of the 1st petitioner.

2nd and 4th petitioners are the brothers of the 1st petitioner,
3rd and 5th petitioners are the wives of the 2nd and 4th petitioners respectively.
3. The allegation against the petitioners is as follows: the marriage between the 1st petitioner/1st accused and the defacto complainant was solemnized on 06.10.2019.
Thereafter, they started their marital life at the residence of the 1 st petitioner.
Later, they shifted to Bahrain, where the 1st petitioner was working.
While so, the 1st petitioner allegedly obtained an amount of Rs. 20 lakhs and 103 sovereigns of gold ornaments of the victim, which was misappropriated by him.
It was also alleged that, on several occasions, the defacto complainant was subjected to ill-treatment mentally and physically by the petitioners by demanding more amounts as dowry.
A complaint was submitted in such circumstances.
This application for anticipatory bail is submitted as they apprehend arrest.

4. Heard, Sri. C.P. Udayabhanu, the learned counsel appearing for the petitioners and Sri.M.P.Prasanth, the learned Public Prosecutor, appearing for the State.
5.
The learned counsel for the petitioners submits that the crime was registered based on false allegations.
Certain matrimonial disputes are pending between the 1 st petitioner and the defacto complainant.
On account of the same, a false complaint was submitted, contends the learned counsel.
It is further pointed out that the petitioners are prepared to abide by any conditions that may be imposed by this Court and are willing to cooperate with the investigation.
6. On the other hand, the learned Public Prosecutor would oppose the aforesaid bail application.
It is pointed out that there are allegations of ill-treatment made by the petitioners herein, and the matter is under investigation.
It is also contended that if the petitioners were granted anticipatory bail, it would affect the investigation, which is in progress.
7. I have gone through the records and heard the contentions raised from both sides.

On going through the records, it is discernible that, even though certain allegations of ill treatment have been made, no specific instances are stated by the defacto complainant, instead, it contains general statements.
On going through the Annexure-2 complaint, it can be seen that the main grievances are pertaining to the alleged appropriation of the amount and gold ornaments by the petitioners herein.
There are several litigations pending between the parties before the Family Court concerned.
In such circumstances, I do not find any necessity for custodial interrogation of the petitioners.
8. Considering the facts and circumstances of the case, I am of the view that the purpose would be served if the cooperation of the petitioners with the investigation is ensured.

In such circumstances, this bail application is disposed of with the following conditions:-

2 i) The petitioners shall surrender before the Investigating Officer, within a period of two weeks from today, for subjecting themselves to interrogation.
ii) After interrogation, the petitioners shall be released on bail on the very same day of surrender upon the petitioners executing bonds for Rs 1,00,000/- (Rupees one lakh only) each with two sureties each for the like sum, to the satisfaction of the Investigating Officer iii) The petitioners shall fully cooperate with the investigation, including subjecting themselves to the deemed police custody for the purpose of recovery, if any, as and when demanded.

vi) The petitioners shall not commit any offence of similar nature while on bail.

vii) The petitioners shall not make any attempt to contact any of the prosecution witnesses, directly or through any other person, or in any other way try to tamper with the evidence or influence any witnesses or other persons related to the investigation.
viii) The petitioners shall not leave the State of Kerala without the permission of the trial Court.

In case of violation of any of the above conditions, the jurisdictional Court shall be empowered to consider the application for cancellation of bail, if any, and pass appropriate orders in accordance with the law.
